introduction:
A Death Certificate in Uttar Pradesh is issued by the Nagar Nigam, Nagar Palika Parishad, Nagar Panchayat, or Gram Panchayat under the UP Registration of Births and Deaths Rules. It is the official legal document recording details of a death.

Essential for insurance claims, bank settlement, property transfer, pension processing, and succession proceedings. UP uses the e-District portal, e-Nagarsewa, and the CRS portal for online registration.
quickFacts:
Important Quick Facts
  • Purpose: Applying for a Death Certificate online within 21 days of the occurrence of death.
  • Platform: Civil Registration System (CRS) national portal (crsorgi.gov.in).
  • Scope: Demonstrates reporting a death that occurred at home (non-institutional death), though the portal also handles institutional deaths.
  • Target Audience: General Public acting as informants (family members or guardians).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Death Registration

Note: Scanned copies must be in JPG, JPEG, PNG, or PDF formats, with a maximum file size of 8 MB per document.
Informant Details
  • Informant's ID Proof: Aadhaar Card of the person reporting the death (required for registration).
Address Proof
  • Address Proof of the Place of Death: The deceased person's Aadhaar Card can be used.
Supporting Forms
  • Death Supporting Form (Form 4A): For non-institutional/home deaths, this must be filled out and certified/attested by the local Village Head (Pradhan) or relevant local authority on their official letterhead.
Deceased's Information
  • Aadhaar number, Date of Birth (DOB), and parents'/spouse's names are required for entry.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Application via CRS Portal

Part 1: Registration (Sign Up)
  1. Open crsorgi.gov.in (Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome recommended).
  2. Click "Login" in the top right and select "General Public". Click "Sign Up" to create an account.
  3. Fill in "General Information" with the informant's details: First Name, DOB (as per Aadhaar), and Gender.
  4. Enter address details: State, District, Sub-district, Village/Town, and PIN Code.
  5. Enter mobile number, click "Send OTP", enter the 6-digit OTP, and click "Verify".
  6. Optionally enter Email ID, solve the math captcha, and click "Skip & Register" to complete sign up.
Part 2: Submitting the Application
  1. Return to the login page. Enter your mobile, solve the captcha, click "Login", and verify via OTP.
  2. Hover over the "Death" tab and click "Register Death".
  3. Legal Information: Select the State where death occurred. Enter deceased's details (Date of Death, DOB/Age, Gender, Name, and Aadhaar). Enter parent/spouse names and Aadhaar details. Fill in the deceased's addresses and place of death (select 'House' for home deaths). Provide informant relationship and address.
  4. Statistical Information: Select deceased's religion, education, occupation, medical attention details, cause of death (select "Not Stated" if unknown/natural home death), and habits.
  5. Document Upload: Under "Address Proof of the place of death", select 'Aadhaar' and upload the deceased's Aadhaar card copy. Under "Death Supporting form", select 'Form 4A' and upload the Village Pradhan/local authority letter. Save and click Next.
  6. Confirmation: Review all entries and click "Submit".
Part 3: Printing the Application
  1. From the dashboard menu, hover over "Death" and select "Self Reported Applications".
  2. Find your application in the list.
  3. Use the browser print command (Ctrl+P) to print out the complete application form.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Application (Delayed or Manual Registration)

If you choose not to apply online, or if the initial 21-day window has expired, you must complete the process offline.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1 (Visit Local Registrar): Go to your local Registrar of Births and Deaths office (Gram Panchayat office in rural areas, Municipal Corporation/Municipality in urban areas).
  2. Step 2 (Obtain Form): Request the Death Registration Application Form (Form 2) from the office counter.
  3. Step 3 (Fill & Attach): Complete the form manually. Attach original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4 for hospitals, Form 4A for home deaths), ID proofs of deceased/informant, and address proof.
  4. Step 4 (Delayed Registration Requirements): If applying after 21 days, you will need to submit an affidavit from a Notary Public or an order from a First Class Magistrate, along with late fees.
  5. Step 5 (Submission): Submit the physically compiled file to the Registrar for verification.
afterApplying:
After Applying — Physical Verification & Issuance

1. Physical File Submission

The online process is hybrid. You must take the printed online application form along with physical copies of all uploaded documents (Aadhaar, Pradhan's letter/Form 4A) to the local Registrar (Village Panchayat Secretary or Municipal Ward Office).

2. Registrar Approval

The Registrar will cross-check the physically submitted copy with the details submitted online in the system and verify authenticity.

3. Certificate Generation

Once verified and approved (usually in a few days), the official digital Death Certificate is generated. You can download the digitally signed certificate online from the CRS portal or collect it physically from the registrar office.
